name: Smooth SMTP
author: Smmooth WP Plugins

sections.description:
Smooth SMTP gives you full control over how WordPress sends email. Save the sending methods you use, pick a primary and a fallback for when things go wrong, get notified through your preferred channels, and keep a detailed log of every email your site sends.

Sending Methods

Save one or more ways to send email and choose which one WordPress uses. If you don’t choose one, WordPress keeps using its default PHP mail, and all other features still work.

  • SMTP with presets for Gmail, Microsoft 365, Outlook.com, Yahoo, iCloud, Zoho, SendGrid, Mailgun, Postmark, Brevo and Amazon SES
  • Gmail / Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 through OAuth, with more than one account if you need it
  • SendGrid, Mailgun, Postmark, Brevo and Amazon SES through their HTTPS APIs
  • Passwords, API keys and tokens stored encrypted
  • Optional From Email and From Name per sending method
  • Optional routing by From address: an email whose From address matches a method’s own From Email is sent through that method
  • Test any saved method on its own with one click

Primary and Fallback

If the primary sending method fails, Smooth SMTP retries the email once with the fallback. Any saved method, or WordPress Default (PHP mail), can be the fallback, and you can swap primary and fallback with one click.

  • Works whether the primary is a saved method or WordPress’s default PHP mail
  • Logged separately so you can see exactly which method delivered each email

Failure Alert Channels

Get notified the moment an email fails — through the channels your team already uses.

  • Slack, Discord
  • Telegram (via Bot API — requires bot token and chat ID)
  • WhatsApp (via CallMeBot webhook)
  • SMS or any custom webhook endpoint
  • Add multiple channels, enable/disable each independently
  • Send Test Alert button per channel
  • Alerts are throttled to at most one per 60 seconds to avoid flooding

Email Summary Reports

Receive a periodic HTML email summarising your site’s email activity.

  • Hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly schedule
  • Total sent and failed counts, breakdown by sending method, and recent failures
  • Configurable recipient address
  • Send Summary Now button for an instant preview

Email Logging

Every email your site sends is logged with full detail.

  • Status (success / failed), sender, recipients, subject, message body
  • Sent Via column showing the name of the sending method that delivered the email
  • Search, filter, and paginate logs from the admin dashboard
  • View full email detail in a modal
  • Bulk delete, bulk resend, and delete-all options
  • Admin dashboard notice when the most recent email failed

Dashboard

An at-a-glance overview of your site’s email activity.

  • Total sent, failed, and success rate stat cards
  • Breakdown by sending method with progress bars
  • Recent failures table
  • Filter by day, week, month, or all time

Test Emails and Deliverability

Send a test email at any time to verify your configuration, and check the DNS records that decide whether your email reaches the inbox.

  • Test any saved sending method, or WordPress Default (PHP mail), from its row in Settings → Sending Methods
  • Send plain text or HTML test emails to any recipient address
  • Failed SMTP tests show the conversation with the mail server (passwords redacted)
  • Deliverability check (Settings → Deliverability) looks up SPF, DKIM and DMARC for your From domain and compares them with your primary sending method

Other

  • One-click import of email logs from Post SMTP, WP Mail SMTP (Pro email log) and FluentSMTP
  • Option to keep logs and settings when the plugin is deleted
  • Detects other email plugins that take over sending (Post SMTP, WP Mail SMTP, FluentSMTP and others). While one is active, Smooth SMTP keeps logging emails and sending failure alerts, and tells you to deactivate the other plugin to use Smooth SMTP’s sending methods

Privacy Policy

This plugin logs email metadata including sender address, recipient addresses, subject line, message body (unless you turn that off under Settings → Logs), and sending status. Credentials for your sending methods are stored encrypted in your WordPress database. No data is transmitted to external services except to the sending methods (SMTP servers, provider APIs, Google or Microsoft sign-in) and alert channels you configure. The Deliverability check looks up your From domain’s public DNS records.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory, or install through the WordPress plugins screen directly.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins screen in WordPress.
  3. Go to Smooth SMTP → Settings in the admin menu.
  4. Under the Sending Methods tab, click “Add Sending Method” and enter your SMTP, OAuth or API details. The first method you save becomes the primary.
  5. Optionally choose a fallback on the same tab.
  6. Optionally configure failure alert channels and summary reports under the Alerts tab.
sections.faq:
Do I need to enable SMTP for the plugin to be useful?

No. With WordPress Default (PHP mail) as the primary, Smooth SMTP still logs all emails, fires failure alerts, sends summary reports, and uses your fallback if sending fails.

Which email providers are supported?

Any provider that supports standard SMTP. There are ready-made settings for Gmail, Microsoft 365, Outlook.com, Yahoo, iCloud, Zoho, SendGrid, Mailgun, Postmark, Brevo and Amazon SES. Gmail / Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 can also connect by signing in (OAuth, through your own Google Cloud or Microsoft Entra app), and SendGrid, Mailgun, Postmark, Brevo and Amazon SES can send through their HTTPS APIs, which work on hosts that block SMTP ports.

Are my passwords and API keys stored securely?

Yes. Passwords, API keys, client secrets and sign-in tokens are stored encrypted (AES-256-GCM, keyed from your site’s AUTH_KEY and AUTH_SALT) and are never sent back to the browser. If your site’s security keys change, you’ll be asked to enter them again. Where your provider offers them, use an app password, or sign in with Google or Microsoft instead of using a password.

How does the fallback work?

When the primary sending method fails (WordPress fires wp_mail_failed), Smooth SMTP retries the email once with the fallback you chose: another saved sending method or WordPress Default (PHP mail). Both attempts are logged, and the fallback’s entry notes that the primary failed. If the fallback delivers the email, the plugin that sent it is told it was sent (WordPress 5.7 and later), and failure alerts are still sent for the primary.

How do I set up Telegram alerts?

Create a bot via @BotFather on Telegram, copy the bot token, and paste it into the Bot Token field. Then get your chat ID (send a message to your bot and call the getUpdates API endpoint), and paste it into the Chat ID field.

How do I set up WhatsApp alerts?

Register your WhatsApp number with CallMeBot (callmebot.com) and use the API URL they provide as the webhook URL for a WhatsApp channel.

Can I use Smooth SMTP together with Post SMTP, WP Mail SMTP or FluentSMTP?

Only one plugin can send your site’s email. These plugins take over sending (Post SMTP and FluentSMTP replace WordPress’s mail function), so while one is active Smooth SMTP shows a warning, doesn’t run tests, and only logs emails and sends failure alerts. To send with Smooth SMTP, import the other plugin’s logs if you want them (Settings → Logs), then deactivate it.

Can I import logs from another plugin?

Yes. Smooth SMTP can import logs from Post SMTP, WP Mail SMTP (its email log is a Pro feature) and FluentSMTP. Go to Settings → Logs → Import Logs. The other plugin doesn’t need to be active, its logs are left untouched, and logs that were already imported are skipped.

Can I keep my data if I uninstall the plugin?

Yes. Enable “Keep Data on Uninstall” under Settings → Advanced before deleting the plugin.
sections.changelog:
1.3.0

  • New: Route by From address (Settings → Sending Methods → From Address). When an email’s From header matches a sending method’s own From Email, that method sends it. Other emails use the primary, and the fallback works as usual. Off by default.
  • New: A Pro tab on the Settings page describing the Smooth SMTP Pro add-on (delivery status and bounces, routing rules, alerts and health checks), and a Pro link in the plugin’s row on the Plugins screen. Both are hidden once Pro is installed. Everything on the other tabs stays free.
  • New: Until December 14, 2026, a one-line banner on Smooth SMTP’s own screens announces Pro’s launch offer. It can be dismissed, and it never shows on other screens.
  • Enhancement: The email view keeps line breaks in its details, so multi-line errors and add-on details are easier to read.
  • Enhancement: Add-ons can add alert channel types and alert rules to the Alerts tab. Existing channels are converted automatically, and the Telegram bot token is now stored encrypted.
  • Fix: When two requests arrived together right after an update, both could run the upgrade, and the second one logged “Duplicate column” database errors. Only one request runs it now.

1.2.0

  • New: Logs store each email’s Message-ID and the message id returned by the provider, so delivery reports can be matched to log entries.
  • New: Hooks and functions for developers and add-ons: choosing the sending method per email, failure and fallback actions, extra log statuses, delivery statuses, email view details, Settings tabs, dashboard and summary output.
  • Enhancement: The CSV export has a Delivery column, filled in by add-ons that track delivery.
  • Security: SMTP passwords (primary and fallback) are now stored encrypted (AES-256-GCM, keyed from your site’s AUTH_KEY and AUTH_SALT). Existing passwords are encrypted automatically on update. If your site’s security keys change, you’ll be asked to re-enter the password.
  • Security: Saved passwords are no longer sent to the browser. The password fields show a “saved” placeholder; leave them blank to keep the saved password.
  • New: Log retention — automatically delete logs older than a set number of days (Settings → Logs). Off by default.
  • New: Option to not store message bodies in the logs, keeping private content such as password reset links out of the database.
  • New: Logs now store each email’s headers (Cc, Bcc, Reply-To, From) and attachment list, shown in the email detail view.
  • New: Failed test emails show the SMTP conversation with the mail server (passwords redacted) to help diagnose the problem.
  • Enhancement: Resend uses the original headers, so Cc, Bcc, Reply-To and the original From are kept. Resending to custom recipients drops the original Cc and Bcc. Attachments still on the server are re-attached, and missing ones are listed.
  • Enhancement: The fallback now includes the original attachments when retrying a failed email.
  • Fix: Two identical emails sent within a few seconds were logged only once.
  • Fix: A failed test email could create up to three log entries.
  • Fix: Emails with subjects longer than 255 characters were not logged.
  • Fix: The dashboard and summary report periods (“last 24 hours” etc.) were offset by your site’s timezone.
  • Fix: Saving SMTP settings with an empty port showed an “Invalid port number” error.
  • Fix: Passwords containing characters such as < or % were altered when saved.
  • Fix: Re-activating the plugin now restores the summary report schedule.
  • Removed an unused admin page template.
  • New: Email Logs filters for status, sending method and date range, alongside the existing search.
  • New: Sortable Email Logs columns (date, status, sent via, from, to, subject).
  • New: Export CSV of the logs matching the current filters (message bodies are not included).
  • New: HTML emails are previewed in a sandboxed frame that shows the original layout. Scripts never run, and remote images are blocked until you click “Load remote images”, so opening an email doesn’t reveal your IP address to trackers.
  • New: The plugin is translation-ready, including its admin screens, scripts, test emails, summary report and alert messages.
  • Enhancement: Browser pop-ups (alert, prompt and confirm) are replaced with WordPress admin notices and an accessible dialog for confirmations and resend recipients.
  • Enhancement: The “failed email” notice can be dismissed on every screen it appears on, including the WordPress dashboard.
  • Enhancement: Better keyboard and screen reader support on the settings and logs screens (labelled fields, sort state, dialog focus handling).
  • Removed: The “Inspect Post SMTP Table” debug button.
  • Fix: The Add Channel button offered a “Microsoft Teams” alert type that never sent anything.
  • Fix: The “getUpdates” help link for Telegram pointed to a broken URL.
  • New: More sending methods. Gmail / Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 connect with OAuth through your own Google Cloud or Microsoft Entra app (no passwords, no third-party relay). SendGrid, Mailgun, Postmark, Brevo and Amazon SES send through their HTTPS APIs, which work on hosts that block SMTP ports. API keys, client secrets and tokens are stored encrypted.
  • New: SMTP provider presets (Gmail, Microsoft 365, Outlook.com, Yahoo, iCloud, Zoho, SendGrid, Mailgun, Postmark, Brevo, Amazon SES) fill in the host, port and encryption, with setup tips for each.
  • New: Deliverability check (Settings → Deliverability). Looks up SPF, DKIM and DMARC for your From domain, checks that SPF includes your sending service, and warns when the From address doesn’t match the sending account.
  • New: Import email logs from WP Mail SMTP (Pro email log) and FluentSMTP, alongside Post SMTP. Sources are detected by their log table, so the other plugin doesn’t need to be active. Imports run in batches, so large logs don’t time out, and keep each email’s original subject, date, status, headers and attachment list (FluentSMTP, and WP Mail SMTP when it saved attachments). Imported emails can be resent. Imported logs show “Imported (plugin name)” under Sent Via.
  • New: Save several sending methods (Settings → Sending Methods) and choose which one is the primary and which one is the fallback. Any saved method, or WordPress Default (PHP mail), can be the fallback. Switch them with one click, and test each method on its own from the list. Tests use only the chosen method: they never fall back or send alerts.
  • New: Connect more than one Gmail or Microsoft 365 account, each as its own sending method.
  • New: Each sending method can have its own From Email and From Name, used instead of the global From address.
  • New: Sent Via in the logs shows the name of the sending method used. On update, older entries labelled “Primary SMTP” or “Fallback SMTP” are renamed to the method they became, so the filter and the dashboard show one entry per method.
  • Enhancement: Existing settings are converted on update. Your enabled sending method becomes the primary, other methods with saved credentials are kept, and the fallback SMTP server becomes a saved method set as the fallback. Connected Gmail and Microsoft 365 accounts stay connected. A copy of the old settings is kept, so they can be restored if something goes wrong.
  • Removed: The separate Fallback tab, replaced by the primary and fallback choice on the Sending Methods tab.
  • New: A warning on Smooth SMTP’s screens when another plugin sends your site’s email instead (for example Post SMTP, which replaces WordPress’s mail function). While it’s active, tests stop with an explanation instead of failing with a confusing error, Smooth SMTP doesn’t retry failed emails through the other plugin, and the logs show the other plugin under Sent Via.
  • Fix: When the primary failed and the fallback delivered the email, the plugin that sent it (for example WooCommerce or a contact form) was still told it failed. It’s now told the email was sent (WordPress 5.7 and later).
  • Fix: An email retried through the fallback could get other plugins’ changes twice, such as a footer added to every email.
  • Fix: Cc, Bcc, Reply-To and From headers were left out of the email logs, so resends and fallback retries went without them. WordPress removes these headers from the copy it reports; Smooth SMTP now keeps the headers the email was sent with.
  • Fix: When an email failed without reporting a reason, the error shown could be an unrelated PHP message left over from earlier. It now says no error was reported and suggests what may have stopped the email.
  • Fix: A failed test email raised the “Failed to send email” notice on every admin screen. The test result now shows on the Sending Methods tab and in the logs only.
  • Enhancement: Gmail and Microsoft 365 methods that aren’t connected yet have a Connect button in the Sending Methods list, and the form stays open after saving a new one so you can connect right away.
  • Enhancement: The primary and fallback are chosen with the buttons in the Sending Methods list (Make primary, Make fallback, Remove fallback), instead of a separate form above it that did the same thing.
  • Enhancement: Editing a sending method opens its form right under it in the list.
  • Enhancement: The Sending Methods list shows whether each method actually works: “Not tested yet” until an email goes through it, “Working” after one does, and “Last test failed” or “Last email failed” with the error. Before, a method with a wrong API key showed “Ready”.
  • Enhancement: When connecting Gmail or Microsoft 365 fails, the error says what’s wrong and what to do (for example a wrong Client Secret, an expired secret or a Redirect URI that doesn’t match). It stays on the method, in the list and next to the Connect button, until the account connects, and the method’s form opens so you can fix it.
  • Enhancement: The test dialog has Cc and Bcc fields, remembers the addresses you last used, and shows the result in the dialog instead of only at the top of the page.
  • Enhancement: The test email’s last line now says “From:” with the From Name and From Email, and which setting the name comes from. It used to say “Sent from:”, which looked like the sending method’s name.
  • Enhancement: The dashboard, Email Logs and Sending Methods screens fit on phones and narrow windows. Table rows stack, with each value labelled.
  • Removed: The Test Email page. Each sending method has a Test button on the Sending Methods tab, and the deliverability check moved to its own Settings tab. Old links to the Test Email page open Settings → Sending Methods.
  • Requires WordPress 5.3 or later (earlier versions already used functions added in 5.3). Tested up to WordPress 7.1.

1.1.7

  • New: Force From Email and Force From Name — apply your From Email and From Name to every email, even when SMTP is disabled. Overrides From values set by other plugins.
  • Enhancement: Email Logs refresh automatically after a single or bulk resend. Bulk resend lists any per-email errors before refreshing.
  • Fix: Resent and test emails showed “Primary SMTP” in Sent Via even when sent with WordPress Default (PHP mail).
  • Fix: Failed emails were always labelled “Primary SMTP” in Sent Via. They now show the method that actually failed.
  • Fix: Saving the Primary Sending Method tab reset Fallback, Alerts, Summary and Keep Data on Uninstall settings.

1.1.6

  • New: Dashboard page — stat cards (total, sent, failed, success rate), breakdown by sending method, recent failures table, and day/week/month/all-time filter.
  • New: Fallback sending method — automatically retries failed emails using WordPress Default (PHP mail) or a second SMTP server. Works regardless of whether primary SMTP is enabled.
  • New: Failure alert channels — Slack, Discord, Telegram (Bot API), WhatsApp (CallMeBot), SMS, and custom webhooks. Supports multiple channels with per-channel enable/disable and a Send Test Alert button.
  • New: Bulk resend — select multiple log entries and resend them in one action from the Email Logs screen.
  • New: Test Email method selector — test the primary and fallback sending methods independently, always available regardless of SMTP configuration.
  • New: Sent Via tracking — every logged email records which sending method was used. Displayed in the logs table and email detail modal.
  • New: Email summary reports — periodic HTML email summaries (hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly) with sent/failed counts, breakdown by sending method, and recent failures. Includes a Send Summary Now button.
  • Enhancement: Fallback tab copy updated to clarify it works with any primary sending method, not just Smooth SMTP.
  • Enhancement: Added plugin deactivation hook to clean up scheduled cron events.

1.1.5

  • Update FAQ.

1.1.4

  • New: Bulk delete for email logs.
  • New: Search filter on the email log dashboard.
  • New: Pagination with direct page input and Next/Previous navigation.
  • New: One-click import tool for Post SMTP logs.
  • New: Delete All Logs option.
  • New: Data Retention setting to preserve logs after plugin deletion.
  • Enhancement: Color-coded status labels in the logs table.
  • Enhancement: Configurable number of log rows displayed.

1.1.3

  • If sender name or from email is not set, fall back to WordPress site title and admin email address.

1.1.2

  • Commit test email screen.

1.1.1

  • Fix versioning.

1.1

  • New: Test email feature — send plain text or HTML test emails to any address.
  • New: Admin dashboard notice when the most recent email failed to send.

1.0.0

  • Initial release — basic SMTP configuration, email logging, and test email.
